title: Treaty of Peace, Friendship, Limits, and Settlement between the United States of America and the United Mexican States (Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo)
authors: Trist, Nicholas P.; Cuevas, Luis G.; Couto, Bernardo; Atristain, Miguel
publisher_or_journal: National Archives, General Records of the United States Government, Record Group 11
usage: Signature and ratification of 2 February 1848; Mexican cession; Article IX on citizenship; Article X struck by the Senate; protection of property and civil rights.
notes: Exchange copy in Spanish and English; NARA citation and transcript verified. The page records the Senate ratification of 10 March 1848 and proclamation of 4 July 1848.

title: An Act to Execute Certain Treaty Stipulations Relating to the Chinese (Chinese Exclusion Act)
publisher_or_journal: National Archives, General Records of the United States Government, Record Group 11
usage: Ten-year ban on Chinese labourers; certification and re-entry rules; bar on naturalisation; extension by the Geary Act 1892 and repeal in 1943.
notes: Signed 6 May 1882. NARA describes it as the first significant federal law restricting immigration; the Page Act of 1875 had already restricted Chinese women.

title: Executive Order 9066: Authorizing the Secretary of War to Prescribe Military Areas
publisher_or_journal: National Archives, General Records of the United States Government, Record Group 11
usage: Authorisation of military exclusion zones; forced removal and incarceration of about 122,000 Japanese Americans; ten relocation centres; 1988 apology and partial restitution.
notes: Signed 19 February 1942. NARA notes that the order did not name an ethnic group but was applied overwhelmingly to Japanese Americans.

title: Civil Rights Act of 1964
publisher_or_journal: National Archives, General Records of the United States Government, Record Group 11
usage: Title II public accommodations; Title VI federally assisted programmes; Title VII employment discrimination and EEOC; limits of the Act on housing and policing.
notes: Signed 2 July 1964. NARA calls it the most sweeping civil rights legislation since Reconstruction.

title: Voting Rights Act of 1965
publisher_or_journal: National Archives, General Records of the United States Government, Record Group 11
usage: Abolition of literacy tests; federal examiners; Section 5 preclearance; immediate rise in Black voter registration; 2013 Shelby County decision.
notes: Signed 6 August 1965. NARA records about 250,000 new Black voters by the end of 1965.

title: An Indigenous Peoples' History of the United States
usage: Indigenous dispossession as a long structural process; Spanish, French and English colonialisms; Pueblo Revolt; Indian Removal; critique of the 1607 founding narrative.
notes: ISBN 9780807000403. Beacon Press edition verified through Open Library. Synthesis by an Indigenous historian; used for framing and for events where a specialist monograph is not yet in the register.

title: The Half Has Never Been Told: Slavery and the Making of American Capitalism
usage: Slavery as a central engine of US capitalism; cotton expansion; forced migration; the 1619 arrival and the later legal codification of racial slavery.
notes: ISBN 9780465002962. Basic Books edition verified through Open Library. Quantitative and narrative synthesis; some mortality and productivity estimates are debated.

title: Reconstruction: America's Unfinished Revolution, 1863-1877
usage: Civil War as a war over slavery; emancipation; Reconstruction amendments; Black political participation; white terror and the overthrow of Reconstruction.
notes: ISBN 0060158514. First edition verified through Open Library. Standard synthesis; later editions add a new introduction but not a different argument.

title: How to Hide an Empire: A History of the Greater United States
usage: US overseas empire; Puerto Rico, Guam, the Philippines, Hawaii, the Virgin Islands and other territories; the difference between incorporated and unincorporated territory; global base network.
notes: ISBN 9780374172145. FSG edition verified through Open Library. 516 pages; LCCN 2018020388.

title: Strangers from a Different Shore: A History of Asian Americans
usage: Asian migration to Hawaii and the mainland; Chinese railroad and mining labour; Chinese Exclusion; Japanese internment; Asian American communities.
notes: ISBN 0316831093. First edition verified through Open Library. Revised edition 1998; page numbers differ between editions.

title: Impossible Subjects: Illegal Aliens and the Making of Modern America
usage: Construction of the 'illegal alien'; immigration restriction; deportation; Bracero labour; racial and national quotas; citizenship.
notes: ISBN 9780691074719. Princeton University Press edition verified through Open Library. Also relevant is Ngai's 2003 article 'The Strange Career of the Illegal Alien', Law and History Review 21(1), 69-108, DOI 10.2307/3595069.

title: Harvest of Empire: A History of Latinos in America
usage: Latin American migration; Mexican-American War and Guadalupe Hidalgo; Puerto Rico; Cuban, Dominican and Central American migrations; Bracero programme; Latino labour.
notes: ISBN 0140255397. Penguin edition verified through Open Library. Revised edition 2011, ISBN 9780143119289; the 2000 edition is cited.

title: Suffrage: Women's Long Battle for the Vote
usage: Seneca Falls 1848; abolitionist roots of women's rights; Sojourner Truth; Ida B. Wells-Barnett; NAWSA and NWP; ratification of the 19th Amendment in 1920; limits for Black and minority women.
notes: ISBN 9781501165160. Simon & Schuster edition verified through Open Library. Published for the centennial of the 19th Amendment.

title: Death in the Haymarket: A Story of Chicago, the First Labor Movement and the Bombing that Divided Gilded Age America
usage: Chicago labour movement; eight-hour-day campaign; 4 May 1886 bombing; trial and execution of anarchists; memory of Haymarket and May Day.
notes: ISBN 0375422374. Pantheon edition verified through Open Library. Narrative history; the identity of the bomber remains unknown.

title: Tulsa Race Riot: A Report by the Oklahoma Commission to Study the Tulsa Race Riot of 1921
authors: Oklahoma Commission to Study the Tulsa Race Riot of 1921
publisher_or_journal: Oklahoma Commission to Study the Tulsa Race Riot of 1921
usage: 31 May-1 June 1921; Greenwood; destruction of 35 blocks; contemporary death toll of 36 and later estimates up to 300; property losses; historical cover-up.
notes: Report dated 28 February 2001. The official OHS PDF link was unstable when checked; the Internet Archive copy was consulted. The Commission used the term 'riot'; historians increasingly use 'massacre'.

title: Dust Bowl: The Southern Plains in the 1930s
usage: 1930s drought and dust storms; capitalist agriculture and soil exhaustion; federal relief and resettlement; migration from the southern Plains.
notes: ISBN 0195025504. Oxford University Press edition verified through Open Library. 2004 edition adds a new preface; the argument is unchanged.

title: The Rebellious Life of Mrs. Rosa Parks
usage: Rosa Parks as a lifelong activist; Montgomery bus boycott 1955-1956; NAACP and Highlander networks; collective leadership; sexual violence and civil rights.
notes: ISBN 9780807050477. Beacon Press edition verified through Open Library. Corrects the 'tired seamstress' myth.

title: Silent Spring
usage: Pesticide pollution; DDT; ecological interdependence; chemical-industry backlash; influence on the US environmental movement and the creation of the EPA in 1970.
notes: ISBN 9780395075067 for the 1962 Houghton Mifflin edition, verified through Open Library. A historical primary source for the environmental movement, not a current toxicology reference.

title: Stonewall
usage: 28 June 1969 police raid on the Stonewall Inn; spontaneous uprising; Marsha P. Johnson, Sylvia Rivera and other participants; birth of the modern LGBTQ+ rights movement.
notes: ISBN 0525936025. Dutton edition verified through Open Library. Duberman's account is a foundational but partly reconstructed narrative; the 'first brick' attribution is disputed.

title: Katrina: A History, 1915-2015
usage: Hurricane Katrina as a century-long political and environmental disaster; levee failures; racial and class inequalities; displacement; reconstruction of New Orleans.
notes: ISBN 9780674971714. Harvard University Press edition verified through Open Library. Death tolls vary by source (direct deaths about 1,400; total deaths often given as more than 1,800).
